chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who linked it up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him),

He said: The judges are four: A judge who judged with the truth but did not know it was truth, he is in Hellfire; and a judge who judged with falsehood but did not know it was falsehood, he is in Hellfire; and a judge who judged with falsehood and knew it was falsehood, he is in Hellfire; and a judge who judged with the truth and knew it was truth, he is in Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of judges according to Shia hadith and their ultimate fate?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the critical distinction between mere error and intentional falsehood, noting that even a judge who unknowingly rules with the truth is condemned to Hellfire, likely due to the presumption of error or lack of rigorous verification. This classification underscores the high epistemic standard required in Shia jurisprudence, where the judge's internal state and certainty are as vital as the verdict itself. The hadith serves as a stern warning against judicial complacency, emphasizing that true success lies only in the conscious, knowledgeable application of divine truth.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-108 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr who linked it up to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) saying,

“There are four types of judges:1- There are those who unknowingly judge right. They will go to Hell.2- There are those who unknowingly judge wrong. They will also go to Hell.3- There are those who knowingly judge wrong. They will also go to Hell.4- There are those who knowingly judge right. They will go to Paradise.”
